summary: Preinstall alternate-runtime dropper executes obfuscated Bun-bytecode payload
details: Package @servicetitan/anvil2-ext-charts@0.2.5 declares a preinstall hook `node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is hand-obfuscated (_0x-style identifier munging and string-lookup dispatch tables wrapping execFileSync/https.get/readFileSync), platform-branches to pick a Bun binary variant, downloads a Bun runtime archive from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/<platformBinary>.zip into a temp directory, unzips it, chmods the binary to 0755, and then execFileSync's the freshly downloaded Bun against the sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a single ~727KB minified line tagged `// @bun @bun-cjs` (Bun bytecode/bundle format that Node cannot parse), containing a shuffled numeric/string array (n7gIxM), an array-rotate routine (WV8StW), and a base64-alphabet string-array decoder (hc1jfK9) — the standard string-array-decoder loader shape. The package advertises itself as a charts extension and has no legitimate reason to fetch a second language runtime at install time to execute an opaque obfuscated sibling. package.json metadata is empty (`author`, `description`, `keywords`) while the name occupies the @servicetitan scope and references an internal `anvil2` component, consistent with a dependency-confusion / scope-impersonation lure. Installing the package runs attacker-chosen code under the Bun runtime on the installer's machine at npm install time; because the executed payload is Bun bytecode, its behavior cannot be inspected from the Node source alone.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
